title: Valneva: l'Ixchiq contre le chikungunya autorisé au Canada pour les personnes âgées de 12 ans et plus
content: Valneva, a biotechnology company, announced that Health Canada has granted marketing authorization for its single-dose vaccine, Ixchiq, against chikungunya in individuals aged 12 and older. This approval follows the authorization of Ixchiq for use in adults aged 18 and older in Canada, the US, Brazil, and Europe. The European Medicines Agency (EMA) also recommended expanding the vaccine's indication to include individuals aged 12 and older in April. Chikungunya, transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes, causes fever, severe joint and muscle pain, headaches, nausea, fatigue, and skin rashes. According to Valneva, the virus has been identified in over 110 countries in Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas since its reappearance in 2004, with over 3.7 million cases reported in the Americas between 2013 and 2023. The economic impact of the disease is considered extremely significant, said the company. 'This is a significant milestone for Valneva and a major step forward in the fight against chikungunya,' said Valneva in a statement.

title: Vacuna contra chikunguña Ixchiq queda temporalmente fuera de circulación en Estados Unidos
content: On August 26, 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the license of the chikungunya vaccine Ixchiq, one of two approved vaccines, after four serious adverse events were reported, three involving adults aged 70 to 82. The French company Valneva, which manufactures Ixchiq, confirmed the suspension is effective immediately. The FDA and the European Medicines Agency are reviewing the safety data. Valneva’s CEO Thomas Lingelbach said the company is assessing the financial impact of the move. Ixchiq received FDA approval in 2023 and is used mainly in tropical and subtropical regions. The suspension focuses on use in older adults, while the company continues to monitor overall safety. In 2025, Europe recorded 27 chikungunya outbreaks, a record according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). The virus rarely causes death but poses higher risk for infants and the elderly. The FDA’s action aims to prevent serious complications while a strategy for safe vaccine access is developed. Valneva will work with health authorities to determine possible adjustments to authorization and distribution. 'La medida se produce después de informes recientes sobre reacciones adversas en adultos mayores.' 'La suspensión temporal se centra principalmente en el uso en adultos mayores, aunque la empresa continúa monitoreando la seguridad general del producto.' 'El director ejecutivo de Valneva, Thomas Lingelbach, indicó que la compañía está evaluando el impacto financiero de la medida.' 'El virus rara vez resulta mortal, aunque representa un riesgo más alto para bebés y personas mayores.'

title: Valneva confirme l'efficacité de son vaccin contre le chikungunya après quatre ans
content: Valneva, the vaccine manufacturer, announced on September 30 2025 that data from a clinical trial show robust persistence of antibodies four years after a single dose of its chikungunya vaccine, Ixchiq. According to the company’s press release, 95% of the 254 healthy adults who remained in the study had neutralising antibody titres above the seropositivity threshold after four years. The persistence was comparable between adults aged 65 years and older and those aged 18‑64 years. Valneva said the results "are in line with the company’s expectations for this vaccine and confirm a robust and durable antibody persistence in all vaccinated age groups," and that the new data "are also in line with previously published persistence data, confirming once again the key advantage of this vaccine."

title: Westfield Health Bulletin: protecting loved ones from fifth disease
content: The article explains that human parvovirus B19, commonly called fifth disease or erythema infectiosum, is a frequent childhood infection that produces a rash and flu‑like symptoms. It notes that the name ‘fifth disease’ comes from its position as the fifth of the classic childhood viral rash illnesses, following measles, rubella, chicken pox and roseola. The CDC reported an increase in parvovirus cases last year, indicating a rise in the infection’s incidence. While the virus is usually mild in healthy adults and children, it can be more severe in people with weakened immune systems. The article stresses that human parvovirus B19 is not the same as canine parvovirus, which is a serious, sometimes fatal disease in dogs and is not zoonotic. Symptoms in dogs—fatigue, loss of appetite, high fever, vomiting and bloody diarrhea—are distinct from those in humans. The piece advises that puppies that are not fully vaccinated for parvo can acquire the virus in areas where dogs urinate and defecate, such as rest areas and dog parks.

title: チクングニア熱ワクチン、米でライセンス停止「深刻な副反応の症例」
content: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has suspended the license for the Chikungunya fever vaccine Ixchiq after reports of serious adverse reactions. The vaccine, manufactured by France‑based Valneva, was approved in the U.S. in 2023 but has since been linked to four serious adverse events, including three in individuals aged 70‑82. Valneva stated that the suspension is effective immediately, saying, 'The suspension is effective immediately.' Public health experts warn that climate change could expand the range of the mosquito vectors, raising the risk of a future pandemic. The World Health Organization warned in July of a potential large‑scale outbreak, noting that similar early warning signs were seen during the 20‑year‑old Indian Ocean epidemic that affected about 500,000 people. In Europe, 27 chikungunya outbreaks have already been confirmed this year, the highest number on record, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control.

title: リンゴ病感染　１週間で４５人
content: The prefecture announced on October 9, 2025, that the number of new cases of erythema infectiosum (fifth disease or 'slapped cheek' disease) in the period from September 29 to October 5 reached 45, nearly double the previous week's 24 cases. The average number of new cases per medical facility was 2.14, the highest since data collection began in 1999. Health offices in Tokushima, Miwa, and San'yō have issued alerts. Breakdown by health office jurisdiction: Tokushima (31 cases), San'yō (7), Miwa (4), Yoshinogawa (2), Minami (1), and Anan (0). The cumulative number of cases this year is 296, approximately seven times higher than last year's 43 cases. The disease primarily affects infants and elementary school children, presenting symptoms similar to a cold and facial redness. Typically, outbreaks occur around July. The Prefectural Infectious Disease Control Division stated that the causative virus is not effectively killed by alcohol-based disinfectants and emphasized the importance of thorough handwashing with soap.

title: "Effetti avversi", Chikungunya: stop al vaccino Ixchiq
content: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the license of the chikungunya vaccine Ixchiq, produced by Valneva, on 25 August 2025. The decision followed reports of four new serious adverse events, three involving people aged 70‑82, recorded in the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS). The suspension triggered a sharp market reaction: Valneva shares fell 26.07 % at the Paris Bourse, dropping to 3.73 € per share after a low of 3.566 €. Ixchiq had been approved by the FDA in November 2023 and is one of only two U.S. vaccines against chikungunya. The World Health Organization (WHO) had issued an alert in July 2025 after detecting epidemic‑like signals, and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) reported 27 outbreaks in Europe that year. Valneva’s CEO, Thomas Lingelbach, said, 'While we evaluate the next steps, and with the clear threat of chikungunya continuing to grow globally, Valneva remains fully committed to maintaining access to our vaccine as a global health tool to address and prevent outbreaks of this devastating disease.' The company has not altered its revenue forecasts but is assessing the financial impact of a possible permanent U.S. withdrawal. Chikungunya, which originated in East Africa in the 1950s, has spread to over 110 countries; between 2013 and 2023, more than 3.7 million cases were reported in the Americas. The vaccine’s adverse event history includes 17 serious events, including two deaths, in people aged 62‑89, which led to a temporary pause for those over 60 in August 2025.

title: Valneva : Santé Canada autorise la mise sur le marché du vaccin Ixchiq pour les 12 ans et plus
content: Valneva SE, a vaccine specialist, announced that Health Canada has granted a marketing authorization for its single-dose vaccine, Ixchiq, for the prevention of chikungunya disease in individuals aged 12 and older. This announcement follows the extension of the indication to adolescents obtained in Europe in April 2025. The company also highlighted the persistence of antibodies generated by Ixchiq, showing that the immune response has been maintained for 24 months in 97% of participants, with similar durability in young adults and older adults. Valneva aims to create vaccines against diseases with limited treatment options, with a focus on commercializing its vaccine against chikungunya in 2024 and its vaccine against Lyme disease in 2027. The company has a solid financial position, with a net cash balance of €126 million as of March 2025, and is expected to reach profitability in 2026, driven by the growth of its vaccine sales, including Ixchiq and Ixiaro.
